# Proof

We determine $L_{g,h}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{E_g(1,10,n)}{E_h(1,10,n)}$ for $g,h\in\{1,3,7,9\}$.

## Setup

A prime $p>5$ is coprime to $10$, so its last decimal digit belongs to $\{1,3,7,9\}$, i.e. $p$ lies in one of the four reduced residue classes modulo $10$. Thus
$$E_g(1,10,n) = \#\{p\le 10^n : p\text{ prime},\; p\equiv g\pmod{10}\} = \pi(10^n;\,10,\,g) + O(1),$$
where $\pi(x;q,a)=\#\{p\le x: p\text{ prime},\,p\equiv a\pmod q\}$ and the $O(1)$ correction accounts for the primes $2,5$ (which are not in any of the four classes) and for the single prime $p$ with $p\equiv g\pmod{10}$ and $p\le 5$ if any — in any case a bounded, $n$-independent error.

## Applying the Prime Number Theorem for Arithmetic Progressions

The Prime Number Theorem for arithmetic progressions (de la Vallée Poussin, completing Dirichlet's theorem) states: for $\gcd(a,q)=1$,
$$\pi(x;\,q,\,a) \sim \frac{1}{\varphi(q)}\cdot\operatorname{Li}(x) \sim \frac{1}{\varphi(q)}\cdot\frac{x}{\ln x}\qquad (x\to\infty).$$

Here $q=10$ and $\varphi(10)=\varphi(2)\varphi(5)=1\cdot 4=4$, with reduced residue classes $\{1,3,7,9\}$. Each of $g\in\{1,3,7,9\}$ satisfies $\gcd(g,10)=1$, so the theorem applies to every $E_g$.

Setting $x=10^n$ (so $\ln x = n\ln 10$):
$$E_g(1,10,n) = \pi(10^n;10,g)+O(1) \sim \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{10^n}{n\ln 10}\qquad(n\to\infty),$$
and the same asymptotic holds for every $g\in\{1,3,7,9\}$ with the **same** leading constant $\frac{1}{\varphi(10)}=\frac14$.

## Taking the ratio

For any $g,h\in\{1,3,7,9\}$,
$$\frac{E_g(1,10,n)}{E_h(1,10,n)} = \frac{\pi(10^n;10,g)+O(1)}{\pi(10^n;10,h)+O(1)} = \frac{\frac14\frac{10^n}{n\ln 10}\,(1+o(1))+O(1)}{\frac14\frac{10^n}{n\ln 10}\,(1+o(1))+O(1)}.$$

Since $\frac{10^n}{n\ln 10}\to\infty$, the $O(1)$ terms are negligible, and
$$\frac{E_g(1,10,n)}{E_h(1,10,n)} = \frac{1+o(1)}{1+o(1)} \longrightarrow 1.$$

## Conclusion

The primes are equidistributed among the four reduced residue classes modulo $10$. Hence for **every** pair $g,h\in\{1,3,7,9\}$,
$$\boxed{L_{g,h}=1.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
